law: The Core Audio Types framework declares common data types and constants that other Core Audio interfaces use.
Use specialized data types to interact with audio streams, complex buffers, and audiovisual timestamps.
For variable bit rate (VBR) audio, and for CBR audio where the channels have unequal sizes, also use an structure to additionally describe each packet.

Your channels must be laid out in the following order: Left Right Center Low-frequency effects Left surround Right surround Left center Right center An MPEG 7.1-channel, configuration A, audio layout.
